text: dsh-mcp-view 是 DSH Web 的 MCP 工具面板。宿主接口汇总已加载的 MCP 服务器和工具 schema，浏览器面板按服务器展示传输方式、端点、工具说明与参数结构。用户可搜索工具、描述和参数，切换当前会话范围，查看会话日志中的最近使用时间与调用统计，也可探测 HTTP 服务、收藏排序并导出 JSON 或 Markdown。适合需要盘点 DSH 工具和调用情况的 Web 用户；需安装在 Web profile，无需额外 API 密钥。

dsh-mcp-view adds an MCP inventory panel to DSH Web. It groups servers and tools, showing transport, schemas and usage from local session logs. Search names and parameters, switch session scope, check HTTP health, and export JSON or Markdown. Install in the Web profile; no API key is needed.
我想在 DSH 网页里看看当前接入了哪些 MCP 服务器和工具。
有没有地方能直接查某个 MCP 工具的参数结构？
让 DSH 把每个工具最近什么时候用过展示出来。
我想按工具名、描述或者参数字段快速筛选 MCP 工具。
怎么查看工具调用次数和每天的使用情况？
能不能只看当前会话里的 agent 能调用的工具？
Show me the MCP servers and tools currently available in my DSH web session.
I need to inspect a tool's input schema and find tools by parameter name.
dsh-mcp-view 的功能「MCP 清单面板」：按服务器分组展示已配置的 MCP 实例及已注册工具。打开 Web 侧边栏入口查看服务器传输方式、工具数量和端点，并展开工具查看说明与 JSON Schema。
dsh-mcp-view 的功能「搜索与会话范围」：在面板搜索工具名、描述、服务器或参数名，也可切换到当前会话视图。输入搜索词过滤清单；会话范围由宿主解析当前 agent scope 后返回对应工具。
dsh-mcp-view 的功能「使用历史统计」：读取本机 DSH 会话日志中的 tool/call 事件，按工具汇总最近使用时间和调用次数，并提供每日调用与常用工具统计视图。
dsh-mcp-view 的功能「清单导出」：在面板点击 JSON 或 Markdown 导出按钮，将当前 MCP 清单和服务器、工具信息下载为对应格式的文件。
dsh-mcp-view 的功能「服务器健康探测」：在面板触发健康检查后，对 streamable-http MCP 端点发送 HEAD 请求，并在服务器条目上显示可达状态。
dsh-mcp-view 使用历史功能会读取本机 DSH 会话目录中的日志并统计工具调用；扫描受文件数和数据量上限约束。（见 src/index.ts:169-205）

text: dsh-mcp-view README · See every MCP server & tool in your DeepSeek Harness session — right in the Web GUI.：DSH runs your MCP servers (docs, build & analytics — whatever you have configured) and registers their tools into the shared `mcp__*` namespace — but there was **no UI to see them**. This plugin adds a one-click panel that answers: *what MCP servers are configured, which tools are registered, what their input schemas look like, and when each was last used.*

dsh-mcp-view README · ✨ Features：| | |
|---|---|
| 🖥 **All servers, one panel** | Every `dsh-mcp-client` instance in your profile, with transport (`stdio` / `streamable-http`) and endpoint (command or URL), plus connection state (active / disabled / no tools). |
| 🗂 **Collapsed by default** | Servers are folded into a single compact row; one click expands the tool list. `+` / `−` in the header expands or collapses everything. |
| 🧬 **Full JSON schemas** | Each tool shows its raw name, description and the exact `inputSchema` the model sees — expandable, prettified. |
| 🕘 **Last-used times & usage** | Derived from real `tool/call` events in `~/.dsh/sessions/**/session.jsonl[.zstd]` — per tool *and* per server, plus a **Usage** tab with total calls, a calls-per-day chart and the most-used tools. |
| 🔍 **Live search** | Filter by tool name, raw name, description, server **or parameter names**; auto-refresh every 10 s plus a manual refresh button. |
| 🎯 **Per-session view** | Toggle to see only the tools the current session's agent really sees (resolved from the session's agent scope). |

```

Then **restart `dsh web`** and refresh the page — a **「MCP Tools」** button appears at the bottom of the sidebar.

dsh-mcp-view README · Manual (no CLI)：1. Put this package into the profile's `node_modules` (copy, or a junction on Windows):

```powershell
   New-Item -ItemType Junction -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\web\node_modules\dsh-mcp-view" -Target "<abs-path>\dsh-mcp-view"
   ```

2. Append to `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
   - insert:
       - id: mcp-view
         name: 'dsh-mcp-view'
   ```

3. Restart `dsh web`, then **F5** the page.

dsh-mcp-view README · Manual (no CLI)：> The profile patch is watched, so the host half activates live; the client bundle is served fresh at `/plugins/dsh-mcp-view/client.js` — a page refresh is all the browser needs.

dsh-mcp-view README · 🎛 Usage：1. Click **「MCP Tools」** in the sidebar footer (icon-only when the sidebar is collapsed).
2. Browse servers — each row shows transport, tool count and last use; click to expand tools.
3. Click a tool to see its description, full public name and JSON input schema.
4. Type in the filter box to narrow tools and servers; `Esc` or ✕ closes the panel.

dsh-mcp-view README · 🗺 Architecture：| Half | File | Role |
|---|---|---|
| **Host** | `lib/index.js` | `GET /api/mcp-view/tools` returns the JSON inventory: MCP instances from the Cordis loader, live tool schemas from `ctx.tools`, and last-use history scanned from session logs (incremental scan memoized by file mtime/size, 15 s TTL). |
| **Browser** | `lib/client.js` | Client plugin bundle: registers the sidebar toggle in the `sidebar.footer.action` slot and the floating panel in the `shell.overlay` slot. |
dsh-mcp-view README · 🗺 Architecture：No changes to dsh sources — it is a hot-pluggable profile plugin, same mechanism as the `@linxin666` web-ui family.

dsh-mcp-view README · 🔒 Security & privacy：- **Local-only.** Everything runs in your dsh host process and browser; the only network traffic is to the MCP servers *you already configured*.
- **No telemetry, no analytics, no external calls** — the panel never leaves your machine.
- The `/api/mcp-view/tools` route is served by the same-origin webserver; it is **read-only** — it cannot call MCP tools, only list them.
- Last-used times come from your own session logs on disk; nothing is sent anywhere.
- Passwords / credentials of your MCP servers are **never** exposed — only transport type and endpoint URL.

dsh-mcp-view README · 🧩 Compatibility：- `@deepseek-ai/dsh` `0.1.0-rc.6` (web profile) — same cadence as the ecosystem's pinned SDK versions.
- Node `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` (the dsh runtime requirement — zstd session decoding is used).
- Browser: Chrome / Edge / Firefox (React 18, no build step for the client bundle).

dsh-mcp-view README · ❓ FAQ：**Are MCP servers per-session or shared?**
Shared. MCP servers are configured once at the profile level (`cordis.patch.yml`), connect once per process, and register their tools into the process-wide `ToolRuntime` — every session and workspace sees the same set. A session whose agent preset restricts tools may hide them *from the model*, but the registry stays global.

dsh-mcp-view README · ❓ FAQ：**Where does «used …» come from?**
From `tool/call` events in your persisted session logs (`~/.dsh/sessions`). It is the real dispatch timestamp of the last call of that tool. If the log has no calls for a tool, the hint is simply absent.

**Why are only some tools listed under "Other tools"?**
The panel shows the *global* registry. Per-session agent tools (e.g. `pwsh`, `read`) register in the session's scope layer, so they are not part of the global view.

dsh-mcp-view README · ❓ FAQ：**Does the panel slow things down?**
No. The session scan is incremental (only changed files are re-read) and rate-limited to once per 15 s; the browser auto-refresh is 10 s.
